title: Summary
content:
# B.2.3 Summary

The canvas below summarises the impact pathway and the measures that carry it. One design choice runs through every cell: a single agricultural pressure gradient, from farmland, through the freshwater ecotones that receive its runoff, to the coastal waters downstream. Each result maps to a topic outcome first, then to a destination impact, as B.2.1 sets out.

## Impact canvas

### Upper row

| Specific needs | Expected results | Dissemination, exploitation and communication measures |
|---|---|---|
| Biodiversity data exists in quantity and integrates badly. Many in-situ collections "were not designed with Satellite Remote Sensing integration in mind" and "lack the structure, interface and metadata required to support advanced analytics, including AI". Today the reconciliation of molecular, plot, airborne and satellite evidence is done once per project and discarded. Assessment and trend prediction need fit-for-purpose, interoperable data across the terrestrial, freshwater and marine realms (SR-01, SR-02). | One reusable observation chain carries measurement from molecules to satellites along the gradient. It is released as the Multisensory integration architecture specification (D2.2), the Joint data collection, metadata and processing protocols (D3.1), the Interoperability crosswalk package (D3.2) and the Provenance-tracked processing pipeline release (D3.3). It yields the Documented training and validation resource with split protocol (D6.1), the Habitat and ecosystem classification models and benchmarks (D6.2), the European-scale maps and biodiversity trend predictions (D6.3), the Genome-to-space linkage report (D5.3) and the Biodiversity indicator decision-support release (D7.2). | One work package, Policy uptake, sectoral mainstreaming and exploitation (WP7), carries all three functions, consolidated in the Dissemination, exploitation and communication plan (D7.4). The Data management plan and shared metadata profile (D1.1) fixes the open-data commitments. Dissemination releases the protocols, crosswalks, pipeline, training resource and models under FAIR terms to the European Open Science Cloud and the common data spaces. Exploitation submits the harmonisation decisions to the standards bodies, recorded in the FAIR publication and standards contribution report (D3.4), and carries indicators into farm-management tools. Communication delivers plain-language evidence on the land-to-coast pressure pathway. |

### Lower row

| Target groups | Outcomes | Impacts |
|---|---|---|
| Ecosystem-assessment and biodiversity machine-learning research groups. Biodiversity data-infrastructure operators and the standards bodies that maintain the European habitat classification and the global ecosystem typology. Competent authorities carrying EU biodiversity-reporting obligations. Farmers, land and sea managers, and the agricultural holdings reached through a multi-country user network. The international biodiversity assessment community. Policymakers and the public. | OC1: one multisensory integration architecture carries omics, in-situ, airborne and satellite observation. OC2: joint protocols, a crosswalk package and a provenance-tracked pipeline make the harmonisation decisions usable outside the project and reach the standards bodies. OC3: three cases on one gradient produce comparable datasets across the three realms, with a report on which decisions survived transfer. OC4: the molecular layer joins the in-situ and remote-sensing record through a published metadata standard. OC5: a documented training and validation resource lets an external group reproduce the benchmarks. OC6: classification runs at European coverage and trend predictions carry measured uncertainty. OC7: authorities receive outputs shaped to their reporting obligations and holdings receive indicators inside their own tools. | Destination Biodiversity and ecosystem services. EI-01: knowledge on biodiversity status, trends and drivers improves. EI-02: methods, models and tools are available and used. EI-03: the biodiversity crisis is better understood. EI-04: policymakers, economic sectors and society are better informed, toward better implementation of biodiversity legislation. EI-05: farmers and managers access information and test biodiversity-friendly practices. EI-06: progress on international commitments is made. |

The measures are proportionate to a Research and Innovation Action of EUR 5,000,000 funding two projects. The project delivers availability and measures reuse rather than promising it. Each impact claim carries one indicator that names one deliverable. No target numbers are fixed yet, because a target is a consortium commitment and no partner's participation is confirmed. The consortium sets them at grant preparation.

Many in-situ collections were not designed with satellite remote-sensing integration in mind and lack the structure, interface and metadata for advanced analytics including AI, so reconciliation is done once per project and discarded.

The central result is one reusable observation chain carrying measurement from molecules to satellites along a single agricultural pressure gradient from farmland through freshwater ecotones to coastal waters.
The results are released as D2.2, D3.1, D3.2, D3.3, D6.1, D6.2, D6.3, D5.3 and D7.2 with those canonical titles.
WP7 carries dissemination, exploitation and communication, consolidated in D7.4, with open-data commitments fixed in D1.1.

Exploitation submits the harmonisation decisions to the standards bodies, recorded in the FAIR publication and standards contribution report (D3.4).
Exploitation carries biodiversity indicators into farm-management tools (O6, OC7, D7.2, D7.3).
Communication delivers plain-language evidence on the land-to-coast pressure pathway.

Target groups are research groups, data-infrastructure operators and standards bodies, competent authorities with EU biodiversity-reporting obligations, farmers and land and sea managers and agricultural holdings, the international biodiversity assessment community, and policymakers and the public.
The outcomes are OC1 to OC7 as stated.
The impacts are the six expected impacts of the destination Biodiversity and ecosystem services (EI-01 to EI-06), set at destination level.
